answer: Quadratic staking erosion forces validators to lock collateral proportional to stake^2, so a Sybil cluster of n nodes incurs marginal cost C=k*n^2 that scales superlinearly. A quadratic slashing rule S=a*C triggered by any zero-knowledge verifiable delay proof confiscates a fraction of the stake, making expected loss exceed extractable value V. The resulting Nash equilibrium reaches its zenith when attackers compute negative expected utility, turning the raven of coordination into a fable of deterrence.
